page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.cm4.2xlarge is an instance within the High Clock Speed family configured with dedicated compute resources. Powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2667 v4 processor operating at a base frequency of 3.2 GHz, it provides 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The system features 32.0 GB of memory, maintaining a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM allocation. No local disk storage is included, requiring network-attached storage for persistence, and no hardware GPUs are present. Network connectivity is rated at a baseline bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Benchmark measurements reflect the operational characteristics of its mature Broadwell microarchitecture. The instance achieved a PassMark CPU score of 8118.07 and demonstrated average throughput in standard utilities, including 26.07 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression and 7.11 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. Because it lacks newer vector extensions such as AVX-512, complex compute tasks show limitations, scoring 1150.0 in single-core and 4273.0 in multi-core Geekbench tests. In addition, large model processing exhibits reduced throughput, registering 11.01 tokens per second for prompt processing on a 7B parameter model.

Memory performance remains stable across standard data patterns, achieving uncached read bandwidth of 39.89 GB/sec and supporting 6.65 million Redis SET operations per second. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance relies on legacy enterprise hardware to deliver predictable CPU cycles and balanced memory capacity. It is suited for moderate enterprise applications, CI/CD compilation, web serving, and in-memory caching layers that do not depend on specialized vector compute acceleration or local high-speed NVMe storage.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.cm4.2xlarge is a dedicated compute instance belonging to the High Clock Speed family, powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2667 v4 processor running at 3.2 GHz. The system provides 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores on an x86_64 architecture, alongside 32.0 GB of RAM, producing a balanced 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio. It lacks bundled local storage and GPUs, relying entirely on network-attached volumes and offering a baseline network throughput of 3 Gbps. Across benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates mid-tier capability in memory-intensive operations, achieving 6.65 million Redis SET operations per second and 7.11 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. However, its older microarchitecture results in lower multi-core and vector compute marks compared to modern silicon. The instance is suited for general enterprise application hosting, standard web servers, intermediate build environments, and basic caching tiers.
